transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE); Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (Borealis Eng Mgr); Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng); Maya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Sasha: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, uh we have about 45 minutes scheduled, we'll do a quick run through of the SDK quickstarts in Python and TypeScript and then Miguel will jump into auth and env setup and we can circle on any security or deployment questions.
[00:18] Aisha: Great, thanks Sasha. We're most interested in getting something into a staging env next week, low latency, and also worrying about cost since we have peak shopping hours.
[00:28] Sasha: Perfect. Quick question on scope — is this primarily a product feature team building a storefront assistant or is it platform infra?
[00:36] Tom: It's product feature with us owning the infra parts — we'll own deployment, but the product folks will own prompts. We want the SDK to be easy for both sides, so we need good examples.
[00:48] Miguel: Awesome. I'll start with the Python quickstart, show the install, env var setup, auth, and then TS example. Note that our SDKs are intentionally tiny wrappers around the API so you can copy/paste into serverless or backend services.
[01:05] Miguel: (screen share) pip install redwood-inference, then in your .env put REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-... or for staging use REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-..., we also support scoped keys for route-level limits.
[01:25] Aisha: Quick auth question — we use SSO/SAML via Okta, can we map service accounts to SAML roles?
[01:32] Maya: And from security side — how does key rotation work and do you support KMS/HSM integration?
[01:38] Sasha: Short answer: yes to rotation, support for customer-managed KMS via our Private offering and integrations with cloud KMS. For hosted quickstarts you'll get key rotation UI in the console and a rotating key option plus audit logs. We'll send the security pack with details.
[01:56] Miguel: For SSO you can provision service accounts mapped to SAML groups and then issue scoped API keys programmatically — it's a two-step process in the console or via our control plane APIs. Sometimes the transcription says Sam-El but it's SAML.
[02:12] Tom: Good, we need RBAC and audit logs for PCI scope.
[02:18] Miguel: Yes audit logs and route-level tracing are available, and you can integrate logs with your SIEM.
[02:25] Sasha: Ok back to code — Python example: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2-small', prompt='Hello') — that's simplified, our SDK has streaming helpers too.
[02:47] Miguel: Note about streaming — in Python we have client.stream_generate(...) which yields tokens. For TypeScript it's similar with an async iterator. Streaming lowers tail latency for interactive UIs.
[03:02] Aisha: Are there different models we should pick for cost tradeoff? We will tune for cost during peak.
[03:09] Miguel: Yes we recommend smaller variants for lower cost and fallbacks for reliability. Also use prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts — some of the recorded words show K V cash but it's KV cache.
[03:24] Sasha: We'll include recommended quantization and batching tips in the Optimize notes.
[03:30] [Speaker 1]: uh-huh, and how about embeddings for search?
[03:35] Miguel: Embeddings are a separate call — client.embed(...) — we send batched inputs for efficiency. For TS we demo fetch('/v1/embeddings', ...) example and SDK wrapper.
[03:46] Tom: On environment setup — do you recommend server-side only keys or client-side?
[03:50] Miguel: Server-side only for all write/generation calls. If you need client access for limited features, use short-lived, scoped keys or a proxy token. We don't recommend exposing long-lived keys in the browser.
[04:05] Aisha: Can you show the TS quickstart?
[04:08] Miguel: Sure. npm i @redwood/inference, in a Next.js API route you do import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-2-chat', messages: [...] });
[04:28] Miguel: Small gotcha: some examples in docs used REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY, there was a mismatch — we've standardized to REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[04:36] Sasha: That's a good callout — we'll update any outdated snippets.
[04:40] Maya: On the network side we need CIDR allow lists and VPC peering options — what's supported for Private?
[04:47] Sasha: Private supports VPC peering and on-prem connectors; for hosted we also support IP allow lists and customer-managed VPN. We'll include the network diagram in the security pack.
[04:58] Aisha: We will probably start in hosted sandbox for dev then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput. How easy is moving between hosted and dedicated?
[05:08] Miguel: Very straightforward — same API surface, you can pin model versions and change endpoints. The routing layer will transparently use your Dedicated pool when provisioned. You should test with small canary traffic first.
[05:20] Tom: For benchmarking, can we run synthetic loads and measure p95/token cost?
[05:25] Miguel: Yes, Miguel (SE) will provide a benchmark script using our SDK where you can vary batch sizes and sequence length; we'll capture latency and token cost.
[05:34] Sasha: I'll make sure to send that script and some sample payloads.
[05:38] [06:00] Miguel: moving on — quick demo of streaming in TS, here's the async iterator pattern, handle partial tokens, re-render in UI as they arrive. There may be small transcription artifacts like 're render' shown as one word.
[06:20] Aisha: Any guidance on prompt caching?
[06:23] Miguel: Use prefix caching for common prompts, and adopt our Optimize recommendations to choose quantized models for non-critical outputs. Optimize can provide per-route tooling suggestions.
[06:35] Sasha: Questions from security?
[06:37] Maya: Yes — retention policies, can we set zero retention for PII?
[06:41] Miguel: For Dedicated/Private you control retention. Hosted supports configurable retention windows and redaction. We'll send the detailed policy doc.
[06:51] Maya: Also need encryption at rest details and HSM support.
[06:54] Sasha: We'll include KMS/HSM integration details and whitepaper.
[07:00] [07:30] Aisha: Ok next steps and success criteria — we want a pilot in staging, 1-2 endpoints, measure latency <150ms p50 and cost less than $0.0008/token average on peak.
[07:44] Sasha: Those are reasonable targets; we'll help set up the benchmark to validate.
[07:50] Tom: Any known limits on concurrency?
[07:53] Miguel: Depends on Dedicated sizing; hosted has soft limits per account. We can propose Dedicated pool sizes after we see pilot traffic.
[08:02] Sasha: I'm going to recap action items — I'll send quickstart repo and README, Miguel will send benchmark scripts and run a paired session, Maya will get the security artifacts, Aisha will confirm stakeholders and pilot criteria.
[08:18] Aisha: Sounds good, we'll try the quickstarts this week and flag any auth issues.
[08:23] Sasha: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and schedule the benchmark.

Meeting close.
